## Goal

As a maintainer of a large test suite, I want to detect near-duplicate test blocks and files, so additive accumulation can be measured and redundant coverage pruned with evidence.

## Problem statement

The test-churn analysis measured large net test growth (+137,022 lines on the reference project) with a low rewrite ratio — the failure mode is additive accumulation, not churn. `evaluate_usefulness.py`'s "duplicate coverage" check is a heuristic and cannot find near-duplicates introduced through different import paths or copy-paste variation. Without clone detection, redundancy grows unnoticed because nothing forces a re-examination.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Detects near-duplicate test blocks (within and across files) using normalised AST/token similarity, not raw text matching.
- [ ] Reports clusters with file, line range and similarity score, ordered by redundancy.
- [ ] Distinguishes legitimate repetition (table-driven cases, parameterised variants) from redundant duplication, and defaults to reporting rather than removal.
- [ ] Emits JSON + Markdown with thresholds and limitations documented.
- [ ] Performance is bounded on a large suite (documented sampling/scope options).
- [ ] Covered by tests; all related documentation updated; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Read-only; no automatic deletion.
- Conservative thresholds; a false "duplicate" verdict is worse than a miss.
- No hardcoded project paths.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — test-value refactor epic (additive accumulation is its stated failure mode).
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — mutation testing; this analyser is a complementary cheap signal.
- `skill/test-churn`, `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`.

discovered-from:SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O

## Notes

Created from the intake discussion on `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O`. Lower urgency than the mutation and assertion-quality arms, but it directly attacks the accumulation problem the epic describes.
data.title: Add near-duplicate test detection to find redundant test coverage

data.description:
# Reduce Large Tool-Call Results Before They Enter Conversation History

## Problem Statement

A single oversized tool-call result (e.g. a 51 KB SKILL.md pasted by the audit skill) inflates the conversation history, causing every subsequent model turn to re-prefill a bloated tail. Measured impact: a 51,945-byte tool message inflated 6,564 to 33,570 tokens across 7 turns, producing 53 s and 72 s time-to-first-byte on a local model measuring 143-303 tok/s prefill. The proxy under-priced the append (173 tokens billed vs. 12,936 measured), making the cost invisible to admission control.

## Users

- **Pi agents**: All agents working with tool results that exceed reasonable sizes (skill bodies, large file reads, JSON dumps) will benefit from automatic result reduction.
- **Operators**: Reduced prefill times mean faster response cycles and lower GPU contention.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A measurement report exists ranking tool-result payload size by tool and session, produced by a committed deterministic script (no model calls), with the top offenders named.
- AC2: Each of the five candidate approaches is assessed for (a) bytes/tokens saved, (b) added latency and GPU contention, (c) information-loss risk and recoverability, with a recorded recommendation.
- AC3: At least one non-model mechanism (truncate-with-re-read or reference-instead-of-inline) is prototyped as a Pi extension and validated against a real oversized tool result, with the before/after prompt-token counts recorded.
- AC4: If a small-model compaction path is implemented, it reuses the existing summariser slot (Qwen2.5-7B preset, parallel=1), is benchmarked against the prefill cost it avoids, and includes a documented fallback when the summariser is unavailable.
- AC5: Documentation states the extension's threshold, behaviour and how an agent recovers truncated content, and the result is recorded against the originating LLM-repo prefill-pricing item.

## Impact

Agents experience faster response times when working with tool results, as oversized payloads are automatically reduced before entering conversation history, avoiding 50+ second prefill delays on subsequent turns.

## Constraints

- Compaction must be cheaper than the prefill it avoids. A ~2 s small-model call must avoid 45-90 s of prefill (saving ~13k tokens at 143-303 tok/s).
- Any lossy step must be recoverable — raw payload retained and re-readable via `offset`/`limit` parameters.
- Runs on the same GPU as the workload it protects; competes for capacity, hence the preference for non-model approaches first.
- Must not alter the tool-call contract — agents must still be able to read content they couldn't fit in one call.

## Candidate Approaches (cheapest first)

1. **Measure first** — rank tool results by bytes/tokens across recorded sessions (deterministic script, no model calls).
2. **Truncate with re-read** — Pi extension intercepts oversized tool results, keeps head/tail, preserves raw output on disk with a re-read marker.
3. **Reference instead of inline** — content-address large or repeated payloads (skill bodies, already-read files), substitute a short handle plus preview.
4. **Small-model compaction** — detect oversized tool results, ask a small model (Qwen2.5-7B summariser slot) to compact them. Escalate only when approaches 2 and 3 are insufficient.
5. **Structured projections** — JSON field selection, summary-by-default with details on demand, at the tool level.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `command/pi.mjs` or equivalent — where tool-call results enter the conversation
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` or audit skill scripts — source of one measured oversized payload
- `~/.llm-proxy/session-recordings/` — session recordings for measurement analysis
- `~/.pi/agent/sessions/` — session jsonl files for measurement analysis
- Pi extension framework files — for the truncation/reference implementation

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep**: Five candidate approaches could tempt implementing all of them. Risk: scope expansion. Mitigation: implement one non-model mechanism for AC3; assess all five for AC2; defer small-model compaction unless validated as necessary.
- **Threshold selection**: The truncation threshold (AC3) must be chosen carefully — too aggressive loses useful content, too permissive doesn't solve the problem. Risk: wrong default. Mitigation: measurement report (AC1) informs threshold; make it configurable.
- **Agent confusion**: Agents may not understand truncation markers or how to re-read content. Risk: agent errors. Mitigation: clear documentation (AC5); test with real agent sessions.
- **GPU contention**: Approach 4 (small-model compaction) competes for the same GPU. Risk: compaction takes longer than prefill savings. Mitigation: benchmark against prefill cost (AC4); fallback to no-op when summariser unavailable.
- **Assumption**: Session recordings at `~/.llm-proxy/session-recordings/` and `~/.pi/agent/sessions/` are available for measurement analysis. If not accessible, the measurement script (AC1) should gracefully handle this.

## Related Work

- Originating evidence: LLM-repo worklog items LP-0MW0KZUUS002LICZ (prefill pricing) and LP-0MW0KZV5H004Z4UI.
- Session recordings at `~/.llm-proxy/session-recordings/` and session jsonl files at `~/.pi/agent/sessions/`.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: Should this work be implemented in the SorraAgents repo or the LLM proxy repo? — Answer (agent@herdr): The Pi extension prototype should live in SorraAgents (where Pi extensions are managed), but the measurement script and documentation should link back to the LLM-repo prefill-pricing items. Source: intake assessment.
- Q: What threshold should trigger truncation? — Answer (agent@herdr): TBD — the measurement report (AC1) will inform a data-driven threshold. A reasonable starting point for prototyping is 10 KB or ~5,000 tokens. Source: intake assessment, to be confirmed by measurement.
- Q: Should the extension handle both text and binary results? — Answer (agent@herdr): Focus on text-based results (file reads, tool output) for AC3; binary handling can be deferred to implementation. Source: intake assessment.
data.title: Reduce large tool-call results before they enter conversation history

## Problem

`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:_resolve_merge_base()` returns the **candidate ref name** (`origin/dev`) rather than the SHA resolved by `git merge-base`, and `compute_changed_files()` then runs `git diff --name-only <ref>` against that name.

When an implement worktree's branch base is *behind* the ref (a stale base — e.g. the branch was forked while local `dev` lagged `origin/dev`), diffing against the ref includes **dev-side** commits that are not part of the change set. `select_group_from_changed_files()` then picks test groups for unrelated work.

Discovered-from: WL-0MW3LTY9A007ZULJ (ContextHub store) — the stale-base session in which this was observed.

## Evidence

- Observed on 2026-11-05 in a ContextHub implement session (WL-0MW3JIYIR002RCP8): a docs + `tests/setup-tests.ts` change set ran `npm test -- packages/herdr/src` because the stale base made the diff include dev-side `packages/herdr` commits.
- Current code (`run_tests.py`, `_resolve_merge_base`, ~line 506): the loop runs `git merge-base <candidate> HEAD`, then `return candidate` (the ref name) — the resolved `proc.stdout.strip()` SHA is discarded.
- `compute_changed_files()` (~line 462) passes the returned value straight into `git diff --name-only <base>`.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** running `implement.py finish` / `run_tests.py --scope changed` — depend on correct changed-file selection.
- **Operators / CI** — depend on changed-scope runs exercising the code that actually changed.

### Example user stories

- As an implementation agent, when my worktree forked from a base behind `origin/dev`, I want changed-scope selection to measure only *my* diff, so the gate runs the right tests.
- As an operator, I want a stale base to degrade into a smaller diff, never into an unrelated named group.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `_resolve_merge_base()` returns the SHA resolved by `git merge-base` (falling back to the next candidate only when `merge-base` yields nothing), never a bare ref name.
- [ ] `compute_changed_files()` diffs against a merge-base SHA, so commits that exist on the ref but not on the branch base are excluded from the change set.
- [ ] Regression test: a fixture repo whose branch base is one commit behind the target ref — the changed-file set must contain only the branch's own files, not the ref-side files.
- [ ] Fallback behaviour preserved: with no usable base the function still returns `None` and callers fall back to full scope (no crash).
- [ ] Documentation updated where the changed-scope base semantics are described (`skill/test/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`) if the returned value's contract changes.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Probe/read-only of git state; no new runtime dependencies; reuse existing helpers (`_git_inspection_env`, `run_cmd`).
- Behaviour change must be conservative: an unresolved base must still fall back to full scope rather than an empty diff.
- Related but distinct from SA-0MUH1P93R006NT66 (unqualified `origin/dev` ref *ambiguity* with a shadowing local branch) — both live in the same function, so either item may be implemented first; if both are taken together, keep the two fixes as separate commits.
- All written output in UK English.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `_resolve_merge_base()` must return the merge-base SHA; `compute_changed_files()` consumes it unchanged.
- `skill/test/tests/` (or the existing test-skill test location) — regression test for a stale-base fixture.
- `skill/test/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — document the returned-value contract if it is described there.

## Related work

- ContextHub `WL-0MW3LTY9A007ZULJ` — Main-checkout local dev diverged from origin/dev (the stale-base incident; records this hand-off).
- `SA-0MUH1P93R006NT66` — Stale local branch named origin/dev makes origin/dev ambiguous (adjacent defect in the same function).
data.title: run_tests.py _resolve_merge_base returns the ref name instead of the merge-base SHA — changed scope picks up ref-side commits

Discovered while implementing SA-0MW3FF18I003KGZE children 1-2 (2026-11-05).

The repository's finish gate and dev-push full-suite runs repeatedly hit the 2700 s per-command timeout under nominal multi-agent host load (full suite observed taking 15-45+ min depending on concurrent suites; verified green runs exist in .worklog/cache). The gate diagnostics classify these as reason=timeout - infrastructure, not code failures - and the documented remedy is to raise timeoutPerCommand in .pi/test-config.json with headroom over a green run's elapsed time.

ACs:
- .pi/test-config.json sets a timeoutPerCommand with headroom over the slowest observed green full-suite run under load (e.g. 5400 s), with the change committed and pushed via a work item.
- A re-run of a previously-timed-out gate for an unchanged tree completes green.

Not urgent (gates converge via cache retry), out of scope for the tracking epic.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MUQ0I0YY000JCB5** – Remove stale references to missing .ralph.json and ralph config system (completed)
- **SA-0MPUDRIHW0024K4M** – Audit runner: read default model from .ralph.json and support --model-source flag (completed)
- **SA-0MPVO6JNI006ESN0** – Triage dev-full-suite failures (run 26780355787) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0mw3ff18i003kgze, acs, agent, cache, change (+58 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: 2700s, acs, agent, cache, change (+57 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: acs, agent, cache, change, children (+57 more)
